## Output writers (`outputs: - type: netcdf` or `pnetcdf`) {#sec-ch15-output}

### Summary

`outputs` is the deck's list of outputs, one entry per writer; an entry holds a writer type, an interval, a list of variables and a few
options that select cells. After initialisation and after every accepted step, each output checks whether its
next time has come and, if so, writes one *frame*: the selected variables of the block, on the block's interior
(or with its ghost zones), optionally cut to a few planes or summed along an axis, as single-precision values
unless double precision is asked for. The `netcdf` writer writes one file per block and then joins the files of
all blocks into one; the `pnetcdf` writer writes one shared file directly. Two statistics variables give the
time-weighted mean and deviation of the state since the previous write. The writers exist so that a run leaves a
self-describing file set, with the coordinates, units and the block decomposition recorded in each file, that
the combine step and the analysis tools can read without the deck.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Writes the selected fields of each accepted state that reaches an output's next time, at the cadence
of @eq-ch15-output-schedule, and joins the blocks' files.

**Data.** Reads the block's `hydro_w`, `hydro_u`, `scalar_*` and user fields through the loaders; writes
`<basename>.block<r>.out<n>.<NNNNN>.nc` per block and `<basename>.out<n>.<NNNNN>.nc` combined (netcdf), or
`<basename>.out<n>.<NNNNN>.nc` directly (pnetcdf), in `output_dir`[^rg-365809d1fc61].

**Placement.** `make_outputs`, called by the driver after initialisation and after every accepted step; the final
call at the end of the run writes no gridded frame.

**Activation.** `outputs: - type: netcdf` (or `pnetcdf`) with `dt`, `variables`[^rg-57a20e47aa5c]; CMake `NETCDF` (netcdf) and
`PNETCDF` (pnetcdf). Default: no outputs.

**Guarantee / limits.** The values of a frame are copied exactly to the host in float64 and stored as float32 unless
`double_precision: true` (netcdf only): relative error at most $2^{-24}$ per finite value, with $\pm\infty$ and NaN
kept. The combined file holds every part's values byte for byte at the part's offset.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of this section, @tbl-ch15-output-tests.
:::

Local symbols of this section: $t$ the time of an accepted state [s]; $t_{\mathrm{next}}$ an output's next write
time [s]; $\Delta t_o$ its interval, the deck's `dt` [s]; $N_{\mathrm{file}}$ its file number; $q_i$ a field's
value after accepted step $i$[^rg-817326ac21bd]; $\Delta t_i = t_i - t_{i-1}$ that step's length [s];
$\mathcal T_i = \sum_{j \le i} \Delta t_j$ the time summed since the previous write [s]; $q^{\mathrm{avg}}_i$ the
running time-weighted mean of $q$; $Q_i$ the running weighted sum of squared deviations [units of $q^2$ s];
$q^{\mathrm{sd}}$ the reported deviation; $N_{\mathrm{acc}}$ the number of accumulated states. *Aliases.* Lane O and its items O6 (the combine)
and O8 (the budget writer, @sec-ch10) in commit messages.

### Derivation

Two rules of this section are stated as equations; the file layout is a convention and is given in the next layer.

**The schedule.** An output with interval $\Delta t_o$ and next time $t_{\mathrm{next}}$ writes at the first
accepted state whose time satisfies $t \ge t_{\mathrm{next}}$, and at that write advances by one interval:

$$
\begin{aligned}
t_{\mathrm{next}} &\leftarrow t_{\mathrm{next}} + \Delta t_o, \\
N_{\mathrm{file}} &\leftarrow N_{\mathrm{file}} + 1 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch15-output-schedule}

@eq-ch15-output-schedule is the body of `MeshBlockImpl::make_outputs`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_output.cpp MeshBlockImpl::make_outputs >}}). Three consequences follow from the
one-interval advance. With $\Delta t_o = 0$ the condition is always true and the output fires at every accepted
state. When one step jumps over several intervals, $t_{\mathrm{next}}$ still moves by one interval, so the output
falls behind the run time and fires at every following step until it has caught up; it never skips an interval.
And an output never fires twice at one time, because the advance happens at the write. A rejected (redone) step
produces no accepted state and so never reaches @eq-ch15-output-schedule.

**The time-weighted statistics.** When `prim_stat` (or `scalar_stat`) is among the variables, the output keeps,
between two writes, the time-weighted mean and the weighted sum of squared deviations of the primitive state (or
the scalar mass fractions), with each accepted state weighted by the step that produced it. They are updated in
place by the weighted form of Welford's recurrence. With $\mathcal T_{i-1} = \sum_{j<i} \Delta t_j$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
q^{\mathrm{avg}}_i &= q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1} + \frac{\Delta t_i}{\mathcal T_{i-1} + \Delta t_i}\,
  \big(q_i - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1}\big), \\
Q_i &= Q_{i-1} + \Delta t_i\,\big(q_i - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1}\big)\big(q_i - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_i\big), \\
q^{\mathrm{sd}} &= \sqrt{\max(Q/\mathcal T,\ 0)} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch15-output-stats}

@eq-ch15-output-stats is computed in `update_weighted_moments`
({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp update_weighted_moments >}}). Why it is the weighted mean and the weighted
sum of squared deviations, by induction in four steps. Assume
$q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1} = \sum_{j<i} \Delta t_j q_j / \mathcal T_{i-1}$ and
$Q_{i-1} = \sum_{j<i} \Delta t_j (q_j - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1})^2$.

1. *The mean.* The first line of @eq-ch15-output-stats equals
   $(\mathcal T_{i-1} q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1} + \Delta t_i q_i)/\mathcal T_i = \sum_{j\le i} \Delta t_j q_j / \mathcal T_i$,
   the weighted mean over all $i$ states.
2. *Shift of the centre.* For any $c$,
   $\sum_{j<i} \Delta t_j (q_j - c)^2 = Q_{i-1} + \mathcal T_{i-1} (q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1} - c)^2$, because the cross
   term $2(q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1} - c)\sum_{j<i}\Delta t_j (q_j - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1})$ vanishes at the mean.
3. *Add the new state.* Take $c = q^{\mathrm{avg}}_i$ and add the new term $\Delta t_i (q_i - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_i)^2$.
   By step 1, $q^{\mathrm{avg}}_i - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1} = \Delta t_i (q_i - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1})/\mathcal T_i$,
   so $\mathcal T_{i-1}(q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1} - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_i)^2 + \Delta t_i (q_i - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_i)^2
   = \Delta t_i (q_i - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1})(q_i - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_i)$, which is the second line of
   @eq-ch15-output-stats.
4. *Start.* At the first accumulated state $\mathcal T_0 = 0$, so $q^{\mathrm{avg}} = q_1$ and $Q = 0$.

Hence $Q/\mathcal T$ is the population variance of the accepted states, weighted by their steps, with no
small-sample correction, and $q^{\mathrm{sd}}$ is its square root.

*Round-off of the mean*, to first order, from the four roundings of one update in `update_weighted_moments`
({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp update_weighted_moments >}}): `delta = value - mean`,
`weight / total_weight` where `total_weight` is itself a sum, the product, and the in-place add.

1. *One update.* The ratio $r_i = \Delta t_i / \mathcal T_i \le 1$ carries a relative error of at most
   $2^{-53}$ from its two roundings, `delta` and the product $2^{-54}$ each, so the
   increment is off by at most $2^{-52} r_i |q_i - q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1}| \le 2^{-51} \max|q|$,
   and the add contributes at most $2^{-54} \max|q|$.
2. *The carried error is damped.* An error $e_{i-1}$ in $q^{\mathrm{avg}}_{i-1}$ enters $q^{\mathrm{avg}}_i$
   multiplied by $1 - r_i \in [0, 1)$.
3. *The weights.* Rounding the running sum $\mathcal T$ perturbs the weights, not the form of the mean; it is
   inside the $2^{-53}$ of step 1.
4. *Hence* after $N_{\mathrm{acc}}$ updates $|e| \le 4.5\, N_{\mathrm{acc}}\, 2^{-53} \max|q|$, a bound
   that is loose because the roundings do not all carry one sign.

The bound is in the unit round-off of the dtype the statistics are kept in, which is `hydro_w`'s (the running
mean is allocated as `zeros_like(value)`); the numbers above are for a float64 state, and a run that keeps
`hydro_w` in float32 has $2^{-24}$ in place of $2^{-53}$. Each state is weighted by the step that ends at it (a
right-endpoint rule in time); the statistics are averages of the accepted states, not of the stage states inside
a step.

**Storage precision.** A frame is copied to the host as float64 by `Frame::to_host`
({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp Frame::to_host >}}) and, unless `double_precision: true`, cast to float32
before it is written, in `Values::put` ({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp Values::put >}}). The cast rounds to
nearest, so a finite value $x$ is stored as $\mathrm{fl}_{32}(x)$ with $|\mathrm{fl}_{32}(x) - x| \le 2^{-24} |x|$;
a value beyond the float32 range becomes $\pm\infty$ and a NaN stays a NaN, because the writer casts in memory and
does not ask the NetCDF library to narrow (which would store the fill value instead). The `time` variable and the
coordinates are written through the same cast.

### Numerical method

**One write.** `GriddedWriter::write_output_file`
({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp GriddedWriter::write_output_file >}}) does nothing on the final call, then
builds the frame in five steps:

1. *Load.* `LoadOutputData` ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::LoadOutputData >}}) collects the
   fields the variables ask for from the hydro, diagnostic, scalar and user loaders; `prim` and `cons` select the
   primitive and conserved hydro rows (`shouldOutputPrimitive`,
   {{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::shouldOutputPrimitive >}}; `shouldOutputConserved`,
   {{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::shouldOutputConserved >}}), named variables select single
   fields, and a field must be one to three dimensional (`appendTensorOutput`,
   {{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::appendTensorOutput >}}).
2. *Range.* `output_range` ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp output_range >}}) gives the interior index range
   of every dimension with more than one cell, widened by the ghost zones when `include_ghost_zones` is set.
3. *Host copy.* `Frame::to_host` ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp Frame::to_host >}}) copies every field once
   to the CPU as float64, shaped `[nx4, nx3, nx2, nx1]` with left padding.
4. *Transform.* `Frame::transform` ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp Frame::transform >}}) applies the slices,
   then the sums. For each axis with a slice list, the cell whose upper face is the first above each requested
   position is selected, positions below the block's lower bound shift the block's offset in the combined grid,
   and a field with one cell along the axis is repeated for every selected plane; when no requested plane falls
   in this block the frame is dropped and nothing is written. A sum adds the selected cells in index order.
5. *Write and combine.* The sink writes the frame; with `combine: true` (the default) the blocks' files are
   joined by `GriddedWriter::combine_blocks`
   ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp GriddedWriter::combine_blocks >}}).

**The frame's grids.** A field's grid kind decides which axes it has: cells (`'c'`), faces along $x_1$, $x_2$ or
$x_3$ (`'1'`-`'3'`), a column (`'z'`), a face column (`'f'`), a horizontal plane (`'p'`) or a scalar (`'s'`), as
`Frame::kind` reads it ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp Frame::kind >}}). `Frame::pack`
({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp Frame::pack >}}) returns one component in the file's order, $x_1$ outermost,
then $x_3$, then $x_2$. A multi-component field is named by its `;`-separated names, or by one name with `?` (or
the end) taking the component number, in `Field::names` ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp Field::names >}});
every name is made NetCDF-legal by `sanitize_netcdf_name`
({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp sanitize_netcdf_name >}}).

**The NetCDF file.** `NetcdfSink::write` ({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfSink::write >}}) writes, for block
`r`, `<output_dir>/<basename>.block<r>.out<n>.<NNNNN>.nc` in NetCDF-4. Its dimensions are `time` (unlimited),
`x1`[^rg-f7f8891d4759], `x2`, `x3`, and `x1f`, `x2f`, `x3f` for every axis that has cells or a slice. The coordinate variables carry
`axis` (`Z`, `X`, `Y`), `units` and `long_name` from `axis_text` ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp axis_text >}});
the horizontal units are `radian` on the gnomonic-equiangle and spherical-polar coordinates and `m` otherwise,
by `horizontal_axis_units` ({{< code src/output/output_utils.hpp horizontal_axis_units >}}). Each coordinate
variable also carries `domain_decomposition`, the four integers `{first, last, start, end}` that place
this block's range in the global axis (1-based on the cell variables; on the face variable of an unsliced
axis `first` and `start` are one less, so a face axis starts at 0), which `NetcdfSink::write`
({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfSink::write >}}) computes from the block's place in the layout; on the cubed
sphere the six panels are laid out $3 \times 2$ in $(x_2, x_3)$, so a panel's horizontal ranges are offset by its
column and row, and its coordinate values are shifted by $\pi/2$ per column and per row, from
`output_block_location` ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp output_block_location >}}). The global attribute
`NumFilesInSet` counts the blocks that hold a requested plane, times six on the cubed sphere. Every field variable
has the file axes `(time, x1, x3, x2)`, a face grid swapping in its face axis, with `units` and `long_name` from
the metadata table when it lists the name; the table, with `rho` in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, `press` in
$\mathrm{Pa}$, the velocities in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and the temperatures in $\mathrm{K}$, is the `MetadataTable`
constructor ({{< code src/output/output_utils.cpp MetadataTable::MetadataTable >}}).

**The combine.** `combine_netcdf_blocks` ({{< code src/output/combine_netcdf.cpp combine_netcdf_blocks >}}) runs
under the per-process protocol of `combine_on_root` ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp combine_on_root >}}):
the blocks of one process count in under the key `output_dir|basename|out<n>|NNNNN` (`ready_to_combine`,
{{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp ready_to_combine >}}), and only the last one proceeds; the process group then
meets at a barrier, the root does the work, and every rank meets again after it, also when the root throws, so
no rank returns before the combined file exists. The root globs the parts (`glob_block_files`,
{{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp glob_block_files >}}), deletes any stale combined file, renames a single part,
or calls `combine_parts`. `combine_parts` ({{< code src/output/combine_parts.cpp combine_parts >}}) takes the
structure of the joined file from the first part, treats a dimension as split when its coordinate variable
carries `domain_decomposition`, sets that dimension's length from `{first, last}`, copies every attribute except
`domain_decomposition` and `NumFilesInSet`, places each part's values of a split variable at the part's `start`
offset in a whole record, writes the whole record once a set of `NumFilesInSet` parts is in, copies an unsplit
variable from the first part only, requires exactly one time record per part, and removes the parts. The
combined file is `<output_dir>/<basename>.out<n>.<NNNNN>.nc`.

**The PnetCDF file.** `PNetcdfSink::write` ({{< code src/output/pnetcdf.cpp PNetcdfSink::write >}}) creates one
shared file `<basename>.out<n>.<NNNNN>.nc` collectively; every block writes its own range at its offset, computed
from its place in the layout. The writer is float only: it refuses `double_precision` at setup, in
`make_pnetcdf_sink` ({{< code src/output/pnetcdf.cpp make_pnetcdf_sink >}}), and again at the first write; it
refuses slices and needs `blocks_per_process: 1`; its dimensions are the whole global grid. Without `PNETCDF=ON`
the type is refused when the block is built, in `MeshBlockImpl::reset`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}); without `NETCDF=ON` a `netcdf` output writes nothing
and returns, from the stub that `netcdf.cpp` compiles in that case ({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp >}}).

**Statistics.** `AccumulateStats` ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::AccumulateStats >}}) starts
the clock at its first call and from then on applies @eq-ch15-output-stats to `hydro_w` (for `prim_stat`) and
`scalar_r` (for `scalar_stat`) with the time since its previous call as the weight, skipping calls with no
elapsed time; `ResetStats` ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::ResetStats >}}) zeroes the sums at
each write; before the first accumulated interval the mean is the current state and the deviation is zero
(`stat_mean`, {{< code src/output/output_type.cpp stat_mean >}}; `stat_std`,
{{< code src/output/output_type.cpp stat_std >}}).

**Which writer.** The block builds one writer per output entry when it is constructed, in `MeshBlockImpl::reset`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}): `restart`, `netcdf`, `budget` and `pnetcdf`; any
other type is refused. The Mesh calls every block's `make_outputs` in block order (`MeshImpl::make_outputs`,
{{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::make_outputs >}}); the driver calls it once after initialisation and once
after every accepted step (the `main` of `straka.cpp`, {{< code examples/straka.cpp main >}}), and `finalize`
makes the final call (`MeshBlockImpl::finalize`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_output.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize >}};
`MeshImpl::finalize`, {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::finalize >}}).

**The final write and the termination reason.** Seven of the ten shipped example drivers (`bryan.cpp`,
`jupiter_evap_precip_1d.cpp`, `run_hydro.cpp`, `shallow_splash.cpp`, `shallow_xy.cpp`, `shock.cpp` and `straka.cpp`) run
their loop while the
integrator's `stop` is false: it stops when `nlim`[^rg-92bdb6d45d3b] is nonnegative and the cycle count has reached it, or when
`tlim` is nonnegative and the time has reached it (`stop`,
[`pyharp integrator.cpp:89-99`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L89-L99)).
A redo result below zero breaks the loop as well, and the driver returns what `finalize` returns
({{< code examples/straka.cpp main >}}). Three signals end a run early. The handler installs itself for `SIGTERM`,
`SIGINT` and `SIGALRM`, and records each in a flag
({{< code src/mesh/signal_handler.cpp SignalHandler::SignalHandler >}}). The flags are read once per step, at the
redo check, where the maximum over the ranks is taken with an allreduce so that every rank stops together
({{< code src/mesh/signal_handler.cpp SignalHandler::CheckSignalFlags >}}; `MeshImpl::check_redo`,
{{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::check_redo >}}, returns $-1$ when a flag is set). `finalize` then makes the final
call of `make_outputs` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_output.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize >}}), which writes the restart
output's `final.restart` and no gridded frame, and `finish_run` prints one reason in this order: the terminate
signal, the interrupt signal, the wall-time limit, the cycle limit, the time limit, or "Terminating abnormally"
when none of them holds; it returns 1 only in that last case and 0 otherwise
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_output.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finish_run >}}). A run that exhausts its redo budget
therefore ends with that line and a nonzero exit status. The three convection drivers (`planar_convection.cpp`,
`spherical_convection.cpp` and `cubed_sphere_convection.cpp`) are outside this scheme: each runs its own loop to a diffusive
end time, treats a negative redo result as an error, writes its own CSV record (the planar and spherical drivers add a JSON summary; the cubed-sphere driver writes
the CSV only), and calls neither `stop`
nor `finalize` ({{< code examples/planar_convection.cpp main >}}); none of this paragraph applies to them.

### Code

**How to use it.** A NetCDF stream every 60 s with the primitives, their time-weighted mean and deviation, and the
pressure, in double precision:

```yaml
output_dir: out
outputs:
  - type: netcdf
    dt: 60.
    variables: [prim, prim_stat, press]
    double_precision: true
```

`output_dir` is the directory every file of the run is written to, taken relative to the working directory and
created when the first writer runs. `variables` is the list of the fields an entry writes: single field names,
or the group names `prim`, `cons`, `prim_stat` and `scalar_stat`.

**Adding a field.** A field is a named tensor loaded into an existing output stream. `OutputType::LoadOutputData` calls the hydro,
diagnostic, scalar and user loaders in that order ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::LoadOutputData >}}).
Keep `type: netcdf` for a snapshot of a new diagnostic: `type` selects the writer, `variables` selects fields. The
procedure below adds a cell-centred scalar without adding a writer.

1. **Choose the loader.** For a case-specific field, register `MeshBlockImpl::user_output_callback` on each block
   before its first output, as the example driver does ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}). Return a map from a
   nonempty field name to a tensor, and select `variables: [uov]` (or `[user_out_var]`) to write every entry.
   `OutputType::loadUserOutputData` refuses a missing callback and appends each entry as one field
   ({{< code src/output/load_user_output_data.cpp OutputType::loadUserOutputData >}}). A built-in diagnostic goes
   into `OutputType::loadDiagOutputData` ({{< code src/output/load_diag_output_data.cpp OutputType::loadDiagOutputData >}});
   a state field belongs in `OutputType::loadHydroOutputData`
   ({{< code src/output/load_hydro_output_data.cpp OutputType::loadHydroOutputData >}}).
2. **Register the selection and data.** There is no separate field registry: `OutputType::ContainVariable` matches
   strings in the stream's `variables` ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::ContainVariable >}}). Add a
   guarded append in the loader body, outside the other keyword guards. This proposed addition copies the total
   density under a new name; replace its tensor expression with the intended diagnostic, and keep the full cell
   array with its ghosts, as the existing loaders do:

   ```cpp
   if (ContainVariable("rho_copy")) {
     auto const& w = vars.at("hydro_w");
     appendTensorOutput("rho_copy", w[IDN]);
   }
   ```

   `OutputType::appendTensorOutput` accepts a tensor of one to three dimensions and adds it to the frame as one
   field ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::appendTensorOutput >}}).
3. **Add metadata and rebuild.** Add `{"rho_copy", "copy of total density", "kg/m^3", "CCC"}` to the table in
   `MetadataTable::MetadataTable` ({{< code src/output/output_utils.cpp MetadataTable::MetadataTable >}}): name, long
   name, units and grid location. The NetCDF sink takes the attributes from that table by field name; an unknown
   name gets no units or long name, and its grid location defaults to cells (`Field::grid`,
   {{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp Field::grid >}}; `Frame::kind`, {{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp Frame::kind >}}).
4. **Select and locate it.** After rebuilding, add a stream to the deck with `variables: [rho_copy]`.
   `OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml` copies the list into the entry's options
   ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}); as stream `<n>` the field is written as
   `rho_copy(time, x1, x3, x2)` in `<basename>.out<n>.<NNNNN>.nc`, or in the per-block files with `combine: false`.
   Choosing `[rho_copy]` before adding its loader branch silently selects no such field.

Check the new field's values, shape, name and units in a written file against the defining calculation. The
tests `UserOutput.registered_callback_allows_uov_output` and `UserOutput.missing_callback_reports_meaningful_error`
cover the callback's acceptance and refusal, not a new field
({{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp UserOutput.registered_callback_allows_uov_output >}};
{{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp UserOutput.missing_callback_reports_meaningful_error >}}).

**What is refused, and why.**

- An output entry without `type`, or with an unknown key (`outputs/<n>/<key>`): the generated reader of
  `output.yaml` ({{< code src/options/output.yaml >}}), tested by `yaml_keys.outputs_refuses_an_unknown_key`
  ({{< code tests/test_yaml_keys.cpp yaml_keys.outputs_refuses_an_unknown_key >}}).
- Both a slice and a sum on one axis, a slice outside `[min, max)` of the global grid, or slices not strictly
  increasing: the `domain` check set of `output.yaml` ({{< code src/options/output.yaml >}}), run for every
  output when the block is built in `MeshBlockImpl::reset` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}),
  so a bad entry stops the run before the first step.
- `pnetcdf` with slices, with `double_precision`, or with more than one block per process; `pnetcdf` without
  `PNETCDF=ON` (above).
- A field of more than three dimensions (`appendTensorOutput`,
  {{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::appendTensorOutput >}}), and a user variable without a
  registered callback, tested by `UserOutput.missing_callback_reports_meaningful_error`
  ({{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp UserOutput.missing_callback_reports_meaningful_error >}}).

**The excerpt.** @eq-ch15-output-schedule, the body of `MeshBlockImpl::make_outputs`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_output.cpp MeshBlockImpl::make_outputs >}}):

```cpp
  for (auto &output_type : output_types) {
    output_type->AccumulateStats(vars, current_time);
    if (final_write) {
      output_type->write_output_file(this, vars, current_time, final_write);
    } else if (current_time >= output_type->next_time) {
      output_type->write_output_file(this, vars, current_time, final_write);
      output_type->ResetStats(current_time);
      output_type->next_time += output_type->options->dt();
      output_type->file_number += 1;
    }
  }
```

: Tests of the output writers and the tolerance each uses. {#tbl-ch15-output-tests}

Every ctest entry of this table passed at the pin on a serial CPU run with NetCDF and PnetCDF built in: 16 of
the 16 tests selected for this chapter, among them `test_user_output.release`, `test_combine_parts.release`,
`test_netcdf_axis_attrs` (both writers) and `test_netcdf_cubed_lonlat_python`.[^ch15-output-run] The
`netcdf_output_without_netcdf_writes_nothing` case is compiled only without NetCDF and so did not run in
that build. The termination test ran at the pin on the same kind of build: `test_uranus_cycle1_abort.release`
passed, with `test_user_output.release` beside it, in a serial run of the two entries (`ctest -j 1`, one run,
one host).

[^ch15-output-run]: [sha: snapy@73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062; deck: the tests' own decks; run: `ctest -j 1 --timeout 1800 -R 'test_options_table|test_options_defaults|test_yaml_keys|test_user_output|test_combine_parts|test_restart_bundle|test_netcdf_cubed_lonlat|test_fp32_restart|test_restart_resume_schedule|test_restart_|test_netcdf_axis_attrs'` from the build directory of a CPU build (`-DCUDA=OFF -DNETCDF=ON -DPNETCDF=ON -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`), one process, the driver tests through `torchrun`; torch 2.10.0+cu128, kintera 2.6.13, pyharp 2.7.17, snapy 2.14.4] All 16 passed. The statistics recurrence @eq-ch15-output-stats has no committed independent check at the pin; adding one
(the two-pass weighted mean and deviation against the recurrence over unequal steps) is a to-do of this section.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `include_ghost_zones` is only meaningful for cell-centred fields; the range widening of `output_range`
  ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp output_range >}}) does not follow the face and reduced grids.
- The `pnetcdf` writer is float only, takes no slices and needs one block per process (above).
- An interval shorter than the step makes an output fire at every step until $t_{\mathrm{next}}$ catches up; it
  does not skip ahead (@eq-ch15-output-schedule).
- The statistics sample accepted states only, weighted by the step that ends at them; stage states inside a
  step do not enter.
- The combine requires one time record per part and the same variable structure in every part; `combine_parts`
  ({{< code src/output/combine_parts.cpp combine_parts >}}) reads the structure from the first part only.
- Signals are read only at the redo check; a rank that never gets there (a hang inside a step) leaves the others
  waiting in the allreduce, and no test exercises a signalled run (`SignalHandler::CheckSignalFlags`,
  {{< code src/mesh/signal_handler.cpp SignalHandler::CheckSignalFlags >}}).
- Only the netcdf, pnetcdf, restart and budget types exist; another `type` stops the run when the block is built.
- Nothing at the pin arms a wall-time alarm: the `-t hh:mm:ss` option is parsed into `wtlim`
  ({{< code examples/command_line.cpp >}}) and read nowhere else, and no code calls `alarm`, so the wall-time reason
  fires only on a `SIGALRM` sent from outside.
:::
